questions.question: Look at this pattern: 10, 15, 20. What is the next number?
questions.explain: Each number goes up by 5, so 20 plus 5 is 25. A common trap is to go back down or repeat the last number.

questions.question: Look at this pattern: 60, 50, 40. What is the next number?
questions.explain: Each number goes down by 10, so 40 minus 10 is 30. Watch out for going the wrong way or subtracting the wrong amount.

questions.question: Look at this pattern: 5, 12, 19. What is the next number?
questions.explain: Each number goes up by 7, so 19 plus 7 is 26. A common slip is to add a smaller number like 5 instead of 7.

questions.question: Look at this pattern: 48, 44, 40. What is the next number?
questions.explain: Each number goes down by 4, so 40 minus 4 is 36. Watch for accidentally subtracting 2 or 5 instead of 4.

questions.question: Maya jumps backward on a number line: 80, 75, 70. Where does her next jump land?
questions.explain: Each jump is 5 back, so 70 minus 5 is 65. A common trap is to jump the wrong way or repeat a number.

questions.question: Dad counts his steps up a hill: 20, 28, 36. How many steps will he be on next?
questions.explain: Each jump adds 8, so 36 plus 8 is 44. Watch for adding a smaller number like 4 or 6 by mistake.

questions.question: Liam has 90 stickers. He gives away 7 each day: 90, 83, 76. How many does he have on Day 4?
questions.explain: Each day takes away 7, so 76 minus 7 is 69. A common slip is subtracting 5 or repeating the last number.

questions.question: At the park, a score keeps going up: 3, 9, 15. What number comes next?
questions.explain: Each number goes up by 6, so 15 plus 6 is 21. Watch for adding 3 by mistake or going backward.

questions.question: Look: 5, 17, 29, 41. What is the next number?
questions.explain: Each number goes up by 12, so 41 plus 12 is 53. A common trap is to subtract instead of adding, or to add the wrong amount.

questions.question: Tom writes: 70, 60, 50, 60. He says the pattern goes down. What went wrong?
questions.explain: The rule is to take away 10 each time, but the last step went back up to 60. The mistake is adding 10 when the pattern should keep going down.

questions.question: Look: 95, 85, 75, 65. What are the next two numbers?
questions.explain: Each number goes down by 10, so 65 minus 10 is 55, and 55 minus 10 is 45. A common trap is to change the rule partway through.

questions.question: A pattern goes 90, 85, 75, 60. What number comes next?
questions.explain: The jumps get bigger each time: down 5, then down 10, then down 15, so the next jump is down 20 and 60 - 20 = 40. Check every jump, not just the first one.

questions.question: Nora has $80 saved. She spends $12 each week: 80, 68, 56. How much will she have after two more weeks?
questions.explain: Take away 12 twice: 56 - 12 = 44, then 44 - 12 = 32. Many children stop after one week and say $44.

questions.question: One number is missing: __, 58, 46, 34, 22. What number goes in the blank?
questions.explain: The pattern goes down by 12 each time, so to find the number before 58 you go back up: 58 + 12 = 70. Going down from 58 gives 46, which is already in the pattern.

questions.question: A pattern goes 2, 3, 5, 8, 12. Ben says the next number is 13 because he adds 1 each time. What went wrong?
options: He added on when the pattern should go down.
He started his counting at the wrong number.
He used only the first jump, not the rest.
He counted the numbers instead of the jumps.
questions.explain: The jumps are 1, then 2, then 3, then 4, so the next jump is 5 and 12 + 5 = 17. Always look at all the jumps, not just the first one.
